pages.text: "Fruit boat!" Bung hid behind the awning, face peeking out. Morning smoke rose. The fruit boat tied to the post beside theirs and stopped alongside.
Bung liked the fruit seller. But "hello" kept slipping back in before coming out. "Today I will," Bung whispered behind the awning.
She passed over two bananas. Bung hid deeper, toes wriggling. Only Ddori sat at the edge, watching her.
She untied the rope and drifted away. Not one word from Bung. Only two yellow bananas remained at the edge.
Bung came out and watched her leave. "Tomorrow... I really will tomorrow." Even hugging bananas, Bung's heart ached.
Next morning, the fruit boat tied up again. Ddori, who could not talk, waved a little hand. The seller smiled and waved back. "Hello!"
She called to Bung across the edge. "A boat arrives? Say hello! Just that." Bung repeated very quietly behind the awning.
Bung took a slow breath, then stepped past the awning. The tied boats lay calm, side by side.
Bung drew Ddori's hand close and stood at the edge. "One, look at their eyes! Two, a little bow! Three, hello!" Bung called loudly, "Hello!"
The seller reached over and stroked Bung's head. One hello brightened the morning. Bung waved with a smile. "Tomorrow too—a boat arrives? Say hello!"
